question: A custom tool's handler only reads data from a third-party pricing API and never mutates any state. The developer wants Claude to be able to call this tool alongside other non-mutating tools in the same turn instead of running them one at a time. What should the developer add to the tool definition?
options: A) Set the idempotentHint annotation to true on the tool
B) Set the openWorldHint annotation to false on the tool
C) Set the readOnlyHint annotation to true on the tool
D) Set the destructiveHint annotation to false on the tool
correct_answers: C) Set the readOnlyHint annotation to true on the tool
explanations: idempotentHint indicates repeated identical calls have no additional effect; it is informational only and does not control parallel batching behavior.
openWorldHint indicates whether the tool reaches systems outside the process; it is informational only and unrelated to enabling parallel execution.
Correct: readOnlyHint tells Claude the tool has no side effects, which is the annotation that controls whether the tool can be batched for parallel calls with other read-only tools.
destructiveHint flags whether a tool may perform destructive updates; it is informational only and does not control whether calls can run in parallel.
